minutes.headline: Planning Board continued the 255 Sunny Hill Road stormwater hearing to Aug 12 and approved the 240 Summer Street site plan and stormwater permit.
minutes.summary: The board heard the 255 Sunny Hill Road stormwater permit. An abutter and a resident spoke. Because a member who joined after the hearing opened should not vote, the board rescinded its vote to close the hearing and continued it to August 12. It then held a new hearing for 240 Summer Street (a contractor's yard). It granted two waivers, closed the hearing, and approved the site plan and stormwater permit with conditions. It also gave a recommendation on a Chapter 61B right of first refusal at 20 Kilburn Street, discussed ARPA project ideas, heard committee reports, and approved the June 24 minutes.

public_comment.topic: No objection to Sunny Hill, but asked that a maintenance easement for the underground drain pipes crossing the lot be put in the conditions; the applicant's engineer agreed.
Objected to the Sunny Hill driveway as too close to water and wetlands, questioned how it could be permitted, and asked that his view go on the record.
Spoke in favor of the character of the Miller family, the owners behind the 240 Summer Street applicant, citing a past kindness to local families.
Said the Millers have been great neighbors and the 240 Summer Street plans look great.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved the site plan and the stormwater permit for 240 Summer Street, a contractor's yard, with conditions; the written decision follows at the next meeting.
The board granted two waivers for 240 Summer Street, on plan scale and the photometric plan, conditioned on shielded, downward-facing lighting with none on the street side.
The board rescinded its vote to close the 255 Sunny Hill Road stormwater hearing and continued it to August 12, so that only members present for the whole hearing vote.
The board voted to recommend to the Select Board that there is no sufficient planning reason to use the town's right of first refusal on 20 Kilburn Street.
Members will send ARPA project ideas, such as a meeting-room sound system and a dedicated Zoom link, to be emailed to the town by month's end.

why_it_matters: The 240 Summer Street approval sets conditions on lighting and stormwater for a contractor's yard near neighbors, and the written decision is what will bind the applicant.
The Kilburn Street recommendation goes to the Select Board, which decides whether the town gives up its chance to buy land under Chapter 61B, and the Open Space Committee may still show interest.
The Sunny Hill Road driveway-near-wetlands objection has not been decided, so residents who want to be heard still have a hearing to attend.
